extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity, academic publishing, and mathematics community (academics, editors, research-watchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A news-style account documenting the retraction of academic papers for ethical/publishing violations, summarizing the reasons, publisher actions, and background. Focused on a specific retraction case in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial overlap / plagiarism without proper citation
rubrics_metrics.description: “The statements in this paper substantially overlap with the PhD thesis of Z. Furdzik … without proper citation.” (quoted from the retraction statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial textual or substantive overlap with prior work, when not properly cited, is grounds for retraction. In this case editors acted after a complaint and independent reviews concluded the overlap and lack of citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to cite unpublished or older theses and non-English sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The retraction cites an unpublished 1968 PhD thesis (in Polish) as the prior work that was not properly acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to cite relevant prior work even if it is unpublished, old, or in another language; failure to do so may constitute improper citation or plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in claims about independent discovery / novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: In a cited passage, Michalik writes that a part of the work was contained in Section 4 and that “the main result is Theorem 3, which was independently proved by the author and Furdzik.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that results were independently obtained must be accurate. Misstating independence or novelty relative to existing (even unpublished) work is an ethical problem and may trigger investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher response procedure for complaints (complaint → independent review → retraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elsevier received a complaint; the editors solicited further independent reviews which indicated overlap; the Editors-in-Chief requested retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers typically act on formal complaints, commission independent assessments, and then editors (often Editors-in-Chief) issue retraction statements when warranted. Documentation of this process is part of due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction statement content and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The retraction statements explicitly state the reason (citation issues and substantial overlap) and identify the prior thesis by title, year, and institutional source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction notices should clearly state the reason for retraction and identify the prior work involved so the community understands the basis for the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that authors respond to inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes: “Michalik hasn’t responded to our request for comment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to respond to inquiries about alleged problems. Non-response is noted publicly and may factor into community perception, though the formal investigative/retraction process rests on independent review and editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper citation practices across related publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2016 paper was cited once — in Michalik’s 2017 paper — where she compared her work with Furdzik’s, asserting independent proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors publish related results across multiple papers, they should correctly attribute prior sources in each relevant paper; referencing earlier related publications does not excuse failing to cite original sources.
